pr_title: Gracefully handle very large sizes on terms
pr_body:
Folks often as for the `terms` agg to have *very* large `size`
parameters in an effort to get everything they can. But they never fill
that large size. They can't! There isn't really enough heap to return
two billion buckets.

After #74096 we try to pre-allocate an array of `size + 1` length,
regardless of how many results are returned. When folks ask for
`MAX_INT` buckets this helpfully fails off in lucene land with an error
message that fairly esoterit to someone reading it outside of
Elasticsearch.

This change handles that `MAX_INT` case by building a
`TopBucketsBuilder` designed to handle large max sizes that are rarely
filled. When you ask for 1024 or more buckets you get that one instead
and we don't preallocate the entire array for the reduction. You get the
old preallocated one when you have few buckets.

Closes #76492

comments: @deathcave can you please give us more information about what operation triggered the problem? Please also check in the Elasticsearch log for any relevant exceptions, and include them here in full.

This was caused by me in #74096. It intentionally skips building the (potentially) long list of results, instead building a priority queue to hold the results so we can skip as we go. That's all well and good, but in your case you get far fewer results than the you request. This used to work because you ended up with a short-ish list and built the queue of exactly that size. You set the size to max_int, presumably because you wanted Elasticsearch to get as many terms as it could or die trying.

I believe I can revive the old behavior.
Opened #76578 which should get you back the old behavior and preserve all of the optimization gained in #74096.

review_comments: I could have made a single TopBucketBuilder which has a buffer and a queue member and flips between them but I didn't feel good making folks that set the size to something low and sensible pay the buffer tax.
I am really curious how you came up with this number.

I looked into my heart and thought "32k is fine to over allocate".  And I thought "this is much bigger than the default of 10 and in the ball park of "too many bars to have in a bar chart". But, fundamentally, it was a guess because I didn't think it was worth spending a lot of time trying to come up with the perfect number. I will add a comment about that.
